articles.title: Why the BAAJA Permitting Reform Bill Is Dividing Climate and Energy Advocates
articles.summary: The Senate voted on Nov. 18 to move forward with the Bipartisan Affordability and American Jobs Act (BAAJA) of 2026, a controversial permitting reform bill that aims to speed up the nation’s ability to build infrastructure and energy —which can often take years under the current process. The bill—which has divided environmentalists and clean energy advocates—will now face a final Senate vote before moving to the House of Representatives. articles.title: The True Story Behind The Altruists and the FTX Scandal
articles.summary: Like other entries in the growing genre of media about tech scandals and leadership crises, Netflix’s The Altruists asks how honest a visionary billionaire can be. articles.title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth May Be Less a Film than a Vibe
articles.summary: It’s easy to feel nostalgia for the Hollywood filmmaking of the 1970s, when wily young directors succeeded in shaking the big-studio money tree to fund their outlandish, and often brilliant, projects. But we’ve also reached the era where the movies of the 1990s look pretty damn good. Which means David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is probably hitting at the right time. articles.title: What the Midterms Taught Us About the State of America’s Democracy
articles.summary: The recent “Blue Wave” was Democrats’ best election night in years. But Memphis, a majority-Black city whose own congressional seat Democrats had held for more than four decades, will be represented in Congress entirely by Republicans . The day after the midterms, Justin Pearson, the Democratic candidate for Tennessee’s newly drawn Ninth District House seat, may have conceded his race, but he refused to concede to the redistricting. articles.title: Amy Poehler and Michael Schur's Dig Is No Parks and Rec—But It's Still a Fun Trip
articles.summary: Dig is sure to catch the eye of anyone scanning for signs of a post-midterms vibe shift. (Never mind that it was announced last spring, just a few months into a second Trump term some interpreted as a long-term rightward swerve.) The Peacock comedy, whose 10-episode first season arrives on Nov. 23, reunites Amy Poehler and Michael Schur , the duo behind the ultimate Obama-era sitcom: Parks and Recreation .
